name: Uncontrolled format string (variable passed as the format argument)
attack_scenario: Attacker-controlled text reaches printf/fprintf/syslog as the format string instead of as an argument; a payload of %x%x%n reads the stack and writes an attacker-chosen value to an attacker-chosen address, giving an arbitrary-write primitive and RCE (classic format-string bug).
negative_test_hint: pass the string "%n%n%n%n" as the message and assert it is printed literally via a fixed "%s" format, never interpreted as format directives

exemplar.explanation: A bare identifier in the format position lets attacker input carry %n/%s directives. Always pass a fixed "%s" literal and the data as an argument. Single-arg printf(x) and 2-arg fprintf(f,x)/syslog(p,x) with no literal format are matched; any call whose format position is a string literal stays clean.
